---
title: List, filter and search
description: Read the items you need from an instance, a page at a time, narrowed by type, tags and properties, or found by the words they hold.
---

An app reads most of what it shows as a listing, and a listing holds only what its credential can read. The examples read a small library of books. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. To keep a listing for every app, [save it as a view](/build/save-a-view); to list events by day, [read a calendar](/build/read-a-calendar); to turn typed names into items, [look them up by title](/build/look-up-items-by-title).

## List a page at a time

[List items](/api-reference/items/listItems) answers one page, 50 items unless you ask for up to 500. This lists the books with the `fiction` tag, 20 items at a time:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.media.book --tag fiction --limit 20
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.media.book&tags=fiction&limit=20
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: { query: { type: "core.media.book", tags: "fiction", limit: 20 } },
});
```

The answer holds the page in `data` and a cursor in `next_cursor`. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor`, with the same query, for the next page.

**Stop only when `next_cursor` is `null`**: a page can be short, even empty, with more after it. A search and a view's items page the same way. The CLI's `--all` follows the cursor for you, and in TypeScript, `pages` does:

```ts
import { pages } from "@withmarfa/client";

const books = pages(async (cursor) => {
  const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
    params: { query: { type: "core.media.book", cursor } },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
  return data;
});

for await (const book of books) console.log(book.properties.title);
```

## Narrow a listing

With no parameters, a listing holds the **active items** of every type you can read, in both tiers. These narrow it, in any combination:

| Parameter | Keeps |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | Up to 10 types, each with every type beneath it. A pattern such as `core.*` matches every type under the prefix. |
| `tags` | Items that carry every tag named: `tags=fiction,signed` lists the items with both tags. |
| `state` | One or more states, such as `active` and `archived`, or `any` on its own. |
| `tier` | `library` or `feed` items. |
| `source` | Items one writer created. |
| `occurred_after`, `occurred_before` | Items whose `occurred_at` falls between two times. |
| `backref[<edge type>]` | The items a given item points to by that edge: `backref[parent-of]=<id>` lists a task's subtasks. |
| `beneath` | An item and everything under it by `parent-of`. Needs read on `parent-of`. |

Over HTTP, a parameter that takes several values takes a comma-separated list. In the CLI, repeat the option:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.media.book --type core.bookmark --state active --state archived
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.media.book,core.bookmark&state=active,archived
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

`include=metadata` adds each item's tags and extensions, so each entry becomes `{ item, metadata }`, and `include=edges` adds its edges.

## Filter by properties

A `filter` narrows by the values items hold. It is one or more conditions of the form `<field> <operator> <value>`, **joined by `AND` or by `OR`, not both**. A property is `properties.<name>`. This finds the books rated 4 or more that carry the `fiction` tag:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.media.book \
  --filter 'properties.rating gte 4 AND tags contains "fiction"'
```

```bash tab="HTTP"
curl -G "$MARFA_API_URL/items" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "type=core.media.book" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=properties.rating gte 4 AND tags contains "fiction"'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: {
    query: {
      type: "core.media.book",
      filter: 'properties.rating gte 4 AND tags contains "fiction"',
    },
  },
});
```

The operators are `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `exists` and `not_exists`. Strings go in double quotes; inside one, write `\"` for a double quote and `\\` for a backslash. For a property that is missing or `null`, use `not_exists`: Marfa refuses a comparison with `null`.

A few fields reach further:

- **`status_group`** tests the group of an item's [status word](/catalog/field-kinds), so one filter spans types whose words differ. `status_group eq "completed"` finds the books finished and the tasks done. It takes `not_started`, `in_progress`, `completed` or `canceled`.
- **`edge[<edge type>]`** finds the items with that edge to a given item: `edge[in-collection] eq "<collection id>"` lists a collection's members.
- **`properties.<field>.<member>`** finds an item by any entry of a list, such as `properties.emails.value eq "priya@example.com"`. It takes `eq` only.
- **`part`** tests whether an item is a [part](/build/edges) of another, such as an attached file. `part eq false` leaves parts out.

A filter holds at most 10 conditions in 2,048 characters. The same filters work in a [saved view](/build/save-a-view), a search and a working copy. The [search and filters](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/search-and-filters.md) chapter of the contract has the whole grammar.

## Sort

A listing comes **newest first**, by `created_at`. `sort` orders it by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at`, `last_activity_at`, the last time the item or one of its rows changed, or a property as `properties.<name>`. `direction` takes `asc` or `desc`. Items that lack a sorted property come last, in either direction.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.media.book --sort properties.rating --direction desc
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.media.book&sort=properties.rating&direction=desc
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

## Find what changed

To catch up with what changed since you last read, list with `updated_after` set to the latest `updated_at` you hold:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --updated-after 2026-11-19T00:11:32.554Z
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?updated_after=2026-11-19T00:11:32.554Z
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

The bound includes items changed at that instant, so **skip the ones you already hold by `id`**. This listing is always oldest change first, so it refuses any other `sort`. A listing can't report a purged item; the event stream can, as [Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync) shows.

## Search

[Search items](/api-reference/search/searchItems) finds items by the words they hold, best match first:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search "le guin" --type core.media.book
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=le%20guin&type=core.media.book
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/search", {
  params: { query: { q: "le guin", type: "core.media.book" } },
});
```

Each entry in `data` holds the `item`, its `metadata`, a `relevance_score` and a `snippet_html`, such as `Ursula K. <mark>Le</mark> <mark>Guin</mark>`. The snippet escapes the item's text and marks each match, so **it's safe to show as HTML**.

**Every word** in `q` must match, in any order, in the item's [searched fields](/catalog/items#searched-fields) or its tags. Words match by their stem, and the last word matches as a prefix, so `le gui` finds results as someone types. Put words in double quotes to match a phrase. A search takes a listing's narrowing parameters and `filter`, answers 20 entries unless you ask for up to 100, and never matches an item in the bin.

`sort` orders a search by `relevance`, the default, or by any field a listing sorts by. In the CLI, a field's underscores become hyphens, as in `--sort updated-at`:

```bash
marfa search "le guin" --type core.media.book --sort properties.rating --direction desc
```

## Count items

[Get item counts](/api-reference/items/getItemStats) counts the items a listing would match, by state, or by type or [source](/build/items-and-types) with `by`:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items stats --by type
```

```text
core.bookmark    2
core.collection  1
core.event       3
core.media.book  4
```

</Terminal>

Over HTTP, a count takes a listing's narrowing parameters, and **counts every state unless you name one**, the bin included.

To count what sits under each of up to 100 items, such as the members of each collection, use [Count item links](/api-reference/items/countItemLinks) with an edge type:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items counts --edge in-collection <collection-id>
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items/counts
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "ids": ["<collection-id>"], "edge": "in-collection" }
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "counts": [
    {
      "id": "<collection-id>",
      "total": 2,
      "status_groups": { "not_started": 0, "in_progress": 1, "completed": 1, "canceled": 0 }
    }
  ]
}
```

## When a query is refused

Marfa refuses a query it can't answer exactly, rather than answer a different one. Each refusal is `400 validation_error` unless it says otherwise:

- **A parameter the operation doesn't take**, such as `tag` for `tags`, is listed in `details.unknown_parameters`. Marfa ignores a parameter that starts with `_`, so use that prefix for your own.
- **A parameter sent empty**, such as `type=`, is listed in `details.empty_parameters`, so an unset variable doesn't read everything.
- **More than 10 types, or `any` beside another state.**
- **A filter that doesn't parse**, mixes `AND` and `OR`, or compares with `null`. The message names the fault and, for an unknown field, the fields you can use.
- **A cursor sent with another `sort`, `direction` or bound** than the query that gave it.
- **A `type` nothing registers** answers `400 unknown_type`.
- **A `type` you can't read** answers `403 type_not_permitted`, and `details.grant` names the type and level.
